verdict.rationale: Osborne Clarke's dedicated EC/VC team says it supports innovation-driven businesses "from incorporation through to exit", and the Flock case shows the firm acting for a client from start-up stage. So incorporation is a first-party offering. However, the page names its core focus as investor fundraising rather than formation, and none of the formation documents are described. Missing for 10: explicit coverage of charter/articles, bylaws, initial board consents and founder stock purchase; evidence that formation is a core part of the practice; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can engage the firm to incorporate my company — charter, bylaws, initial board consents, and founder stock purchase — documented as a core of its startup/emerging-companies practice

citations.quote: support innovation-driven businesses and their investors throughout their lifecycle, from incorporation through to exit.
Osborne Clarke's emerging companies and venture capital (EC/VC) team is our dedicated multi-disciplinary team for high-growth companies
since it was a start-up in 2017, all the way through to its £80m acquisition by Admiral Group in 2026
